summary: Block 12 West -- the 1.6-acre surface parking lot that is the last undeveloped parcel in the Mission Bay South project area -- is the subject of a preliminary, not-yet-approved MOU between OCII and landowner FOCIL-MB LLC to subdivide the site into a roughly 1.16-acre, ~265-unit 100%-affordable project (up to 90 ft) and a roughly 0.43-acre, ~270-unit market-rate project with inclusionary affordable units (up to 250 ft); as of this record's last verification the MOU had not yet come before the OCII Commission for a vote.

milestones.text: The Successor Agency's Approved Long-Range Property Management Plan for Mission Bay lists Block 12 West (APN 8710-006, 'Northeast corner of Channel Street and Mission Bay Drive') among the Mission Bay South 'Affordable Housing Parcels' the Developer (then Catellus, now FOCIL-MB) is obligated to contribute under the 1998 Owner Participation Agreement -- establishing the parcel as a designated future affordable-housing development site years before the 2023 environmental-consultant solicitation or the 2026 subdivision MOU

Mission Bay Citizens Advisory Committee reviews a staff presentation on the proposed Block 12 West MOU and affordable-housing RFP; the presentation states the parcel has 'no entitlements remaining' under current Mission Bay Plan documents and lays out the preliminary subdivision

OCII solicits an environmental consultant for Blocks 4E and 12W to study increasing bulk, density and height limits, establishing that planning work on this parcel predates the 2026 MOU by several years

The August 13, 2026 CAC presentation's own 'next steps' slide targets OCII Commission approval of the MOU for September 2026, alongside a related informational RFP item for affordable-housing development including childcare space; as of this record's last verification, no such vote had appeared on a published Commission agenda (it was absent from the Sep 1, 2026 agenda, and the Sep 15, 2026 regular meeting was cancelled)

facts.value: 385 Channel St (Mission Bay South Block 12 West)
~1.16 acres, ~265 units, up to 90 ft height (preliminary, subject to change)
~0.43 acres, ~270 units with an inclusionary affordable requirement, up to 250 ft height (preliminary, subject to change)

FOCIL-MB LLC (controlled by Farallon Capital Management, successor-in-interest to original Mission Bay master developer Catellus Development Corp), obligated under Owner Participation Agreements to contribute parcels to OCII for affordable housing
Not yet selected -- no developer named for either half of the split parcel as of this record's last verification; OCII's CAC presentation references a forthcoming RFP for the affordable-housing half

open_questions: Has the OCII Commission voted on the MOU? Not as of 2026-09-18: it was absent from the September 1, 2026 agenda and the September 15, 2026 regular meeting was cancelled, with no special/make-up meeting found. Re-check before the next OCII Commission meeting.
No named developer was found for either half of the split parcel; OCII's presentation references a forthcoming RFP for the affordable-housing half only.

No firm entitlement timeline beyond 'environmental review, late 2026' was found; subsequent steps (Owner Participation Agreement amendment, Redevelopment Plan amendment, Design for Development, Blocks 11-12 Major Phase application, subdivision map) are listed only as an ordered sequence with no dates.

No press coverage (SF Chronicle, SF Standard, Mission Local, Potrero View, YIMBY) of the 2026 MOU proposal was found; all substantive detail traces back to OCII's own documents, so this remains a thin, single-source record pending independent coverage.
No cost, budget or subsidy figures for Block 12 West were found in any source reviewed.

No construction-start or completion date has been found for either half of the subdivided parcel, and no expected-completion milestone has been added (2026-09-20 pass): the only whole-plan-area date in OCII's own documents is the Mission Bay South Redevelopment Plan's own 30-year administrative term (Ordinance No. 335-98, effective from Nov 2, 1998), which sets when OCII's authority under the Plan ends, not when a project actually gets built -- using it as a stand-in for a construction-buildout target would misrepresent an undeveloped, still-unentitled parcel as complete in about two years. Left on the 2038+ cap until a real entitlement/construction schedule exists.
